topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and states what students should learn.

topics.label: Genetic and cellular foundations of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as the evolution of mutation-bearing cells whose growth depends on their genetic and cellular context.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence that environmental exposures contribute to cancer rather than its being solely a matter of chance or inherited predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the interaction between infection and malignant transformation.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmental carcinogen-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage that can become cancer-driving mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require subsequent promotion for tumours to develop.

topics.label: Tissue susceptibility within the framework of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consolidate the account of carcinogenesis around the dependence of carcinogenic effects on the biological context of exposure.

topics.label: Evidence and methods for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how researchers identify carcinogenic exposures and evaluate the strength and limitations of the resulting evidence.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by bringing its findings back to everyday decisions about cancer risk.
